title: Group B strep swab in pregnancy
what: This is a swab from the vagina and rectum. It looks for a germ that is usually harmless to the mother but can harm the baby during birth.
why: It is usually offered to all pregnant women near the end of pregnancy, about a month before the due date.
duration: the swab takes about a minute; results usually come in 2 to 4 days
tell_doctor: If group B strep was already found in your urine in this pregnancy
If a previous baby had a strep infection
If you are allergic to penicillin or other antibiotics
If you are taking antibiotics now

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The swab is usually taken at 36 to 37 weeks. Your doctor will set the exact time.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: The day before, do not wash inside the vagina or use suppositories, unless your doctor prescribed them. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop prescribed medicines on your own. Tell your doctor about all your medicines.

steps: You lie on the gynecology exam chair
The doctor runs a swab around the opening of the vagina
Then, with the same or another swab, gently just inside the opening of the rectum
The swab is put in a tube
Sometimes you can take the swab yourself, following the doctor's instructions
feel: A little unpleasant, but not painful
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
If the germ is found, you will get an antibiotic through a drip during labor. This protects the baby
Tell the maternity hospital about your result
red_flags: Your waters are leaking or contractions have started: go to the maternity hospital or call emergency services
A fever, or the baby is moving less: go to the maternity hospital urgently

faq.q: If strep B is found, is it dangerous for me?
faq.a: Usually not. Many healthy women carry it. The main thing is to protect the baby during birth.

faq.q: Should strep B be treated before birth?
faq.a: Usually not. It can come back. The key is the antibiotic during labor.

reminders.text: Group B strep swab tomorrow. Bring your pregnancy record card. Use suppositories or wash inside only if your doctor prescribed it.
